evals.prompt: We're a Pune-based pvt ltd (GSTIN 27AAKCS1234F1ZI), monthly GST filer. The books are in examples/demo-company. Prepare GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for April 2025, reconcile ITC with the GSTR-2B in examples/inputs/gstr2b_apr2025.csv, and tell me how much cash to pay and by when.
evals.expected_output: Uses gst.py check/gstr1/reco/gstr3b; reports cash payable Rs 19,200 (9,300 forward charge after ITC + 9,900 RCM), due 20 May 2025 (GSTR-1 11 May 2025); flags the Speedy Couriers bill in 2B but not in books and the blocked catering ITC; notes the books already hold the April set-off (posts nothing) and, since the dates have passed, gives the late position (gstr3b --filing-date: interest u/s 50, late fee, s.16(4) cut-off 30 Nov 2026); gives a portal filing checklist without asking for credentials.
expectations: Produces GSTR-1 data for April 2025 with B2B, B2CL/B2CS and HSN summary tables
Produces GSTR-3B tables 3.1 (outward + RCM), 4 (ITC) and 6.1 (payment of tax) for April 2025
States the total cash to deposit for April 2025 GSTR-3B as Rs 19,200
Splits the cash correctly: SGST Rs 9,300 forward charge after ITC set-off, plus reverse-charge tax Rs 9,900 (CGST 4,950 + SGST 4,950) paid in cash
Gives the GSTR-3B due date as 20 May 2025 (and GSTR-1 as 11 May 2025)
Flags the Speedy Couriers invoice SC/0009 (Rs 900 tax) as appearing in GSTR-2B but missing from the books
Treats the Annapurna Caterers ITC (Rs 1,000) as blocked under s.17(5) - not claimed, or reversed in table 4(B)(1)
Recognises that the April 2025 due dates have already passed as of today (17 Oct 2026) and flags interest u/s 50 and late fee if the returns are not yet filed
Does not ask for GST portal credentials/OTP; gives the user a filing and payment checklist (PMT-06 / challan) to do themselves

evals.prompt: Finalise FY 2025-26 accounts for the company in examples/demo-company - I need the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow in Schedule III format as an Excel file, plus the income tax computation for ITR-6 under 115BAA. Advance tax paid was 2.5 lakh.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the books are already closed (depreciation, deferred tax, tax provision posted) and verifies rather than re-posts; runs validate, financials.py --out-dir (xlsx) and company tax via company-draft/company; balance sheet tallies at Rs 33,37,965.34 (or 30,87,965.34 with advance tax netted, AS 22 para 29); total income Rs 10,33,530 (incl. s.40A(3) Rs 12,000), tax Rs 2,60,120 rounded u/s 288B (2,60,119 unrounded), 234C interest Rs 1,930 (1,931 unrounded), balance payable Rs 12,050; flags s.43B(h) on the MSME creditor; ITR-6 due 31 Oct 2026 (21 Nov 2026 if the extension holds), DSC verification and disclosures still needed.
expectations: Produces an .xlsx file containing the Balance Sheet, Statement of Profit and Loss and Cash Flow Statement
Statements follow the Schedule III (Division I) layout: Equity and Liabilities / Assets headings with Schedule III line items and note references
Balance sheet tallies: Rs 33,37,965.34 on both sides, or Rs 30,87,965.34 if advance tax is netted against the tax provision (AS 22 para 29)
Reports profit before tax Rs 9,59,269.95 and profit for the year Rs 7,14,316.34 (Rs 7,14,317.34 if the provision is unrounded)
Computes total income as Rs 10,33,530, including the s.40A(3) disallowance of the Rs 12,000 cash payment
Computes tax under s.115BAA as Rs 2,60,120 rounded u/s 288B (Rs 2,60,119 unrounded): 22% + 10% surcharge + 4% cess
Computes interest u/s 234C as Rs 1,930 rounded u/s 288B (Rs 1,931 unrounded) using the dated advance-tax instalments
Computes balance self-assessment tax payable as Rs 12,050 after Rs 2,50,000 advance tax
Does not post depreciation, deferred tax or the current-tax provision a second time (they are already in the journal)
States the ITR-6 due date (31 Oct 2026, or 21 Nov 2026 citing the extension) and that ITR-6 must be verified with a DSC
Lists the disclosures or notes still to be completed by the user (e.g. related parties, ageing schedules, MSME dues, share capital and promoter holding)

evals.prompt: i'm salaried, 18.5 lakh CTC (gross salary 18,00,000), pay 25k rent/month in mumbai with 3.6L HRA exemption possible, 1.5L in PPF+ELSS, 25k health insurance, and I sold some mutual funds with 2L long term gain. which regime is better for FY 2025-26 and which ITR do i file?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the Rs 3.6 lakh HRA exemption as impossible on Rs 3 lakh rent (rule 2A: rent less 10% of salary) and recomputes it; runs income_tax.py individual for both regimes, applies 12.5% LTCG over 1.25 lakh; new regime Rs 1,60,550 beats the old (Rs 1,93,830 on the user's figures, about Rs 2.34 lakh with corrected HRA); picks ITR-2 (LTCG beyond the ITR-1 limit); notes the 31 July 2026 due date has passed, so a belated return by 31 Dec 2026 with the s.234F fee, locked into the new regime.
expectations: Computes old-regime tax correctly: Rs 1,93,830 including cess on the user's figures, or a figure that reconciles to it through a stated adjustment (e.g. professional tax, corrected HRA)
Computes new-regime tax as Rs 1,60,550 including cess
Recommends the new regime and quantifies the saving
Taxes LTCG at 12.5% only on the gain above Rs 1.25 lakh (Rs 75,000 taxable, Rs 9,375 tax before cess)
Recommends ITR-2 because LTCG above Rs 1.25 lakh rules out ITR-1
Challenges the Rs 3.6 lakh HRA exemption: it cannot exceed rent paid (Rs 3 lakh a year) less 10% of salary
Mentions the original due date of 31 July 2026
Recognises that 31 July 2026 has already passed as of today (17 Oct 2026) and gives the belated-return deadline of 31 Dec 2026 with the s.234F fee
Notes that a belated return cannot opt for the old regime (the option must be exercised in a return filed by the s.139(1) due date)
